newsitem.title: MADAGASCAR: 17 candidates register for Madagascar election.
newsitem.headline: 17 candidates register for Madagascar election.

text.p: A total of 17 candidates have registered to stand for the November 3 presidential election on the Indian Ocean island of Madagascar, officials said on Sunday.
They included interim President Norbert Ratsirahonana, former president Albert Zafy, who was impeached by parliament in July, and former president Didier Ratsiraka, the officials said.
Others registering with the high consitutional court were two former prime ministers, a retired gendarmerie general, Desire Rakotoarijaona, and National Assembly President Richard Andrianmanjato.
The deadline for registering ended on Friday and campaigning on the world's fourth largest island starts on October 13.

No woman stood as a candidate. The court says it will issue a list of candidates when it had checked whether they met conditions including a deposit refundable only if the candidate receives a minimum of five percent of all registered voters.
The race is expected to focus on five or six of the 17 registered candidates. Analysts expected many of those standing to lose their deposits because of widespread exasperation with politics.
Retired admiral Ratsiraka, 59 and the father of Madagascar's 1975 socialist revolution, returned to his homeland for the race on September 29, ending 19 months of voluntary exile in France.
Zafy, 70, won Madagascar's multi-party elections in 1993 by defeating former military ruler Ratsiraka, ending his 17 years in power, after an unprecedented campaign of popular protest at his rule.
But Zafy's presidency was dogged by instability, culminating in his impeachment by parliament for violating the constitution.
